event_name: Joan of Arc tried and executed for witchcraft
significance: Joan of Arc was tried and executed for heresy and witchcraft by the English-allied Burgundian ecclesiastical court at Rouen, with charges including communication with demonic spirits and cross-dressing as inversion of natural order; the case illustrates the instrumentalization of witchcraft charges in political persecution and the flexibility of the heresy-witchcraft conflation.
source_method: Trial records published in Jules Quicherat, Procès de condamnation et de réhabilitation de Jeanne d'Arc (1841-1849); analyzed in Cohn, Europe's Inner Demons (1975)
